adrs.name: Version-controlled project truth and machine-local runtime truth
Loopback API and closed permission model
Execution profiles separate from instructions and Skills
Checkout-local daemon is the only CLI execution worker

constraints.name: Human approval and ordered execution integrity
constraints.description: Human decisions and deterministic State and Action gates remain authoritative.
constraints.rationale: The runtime must preserve operator authority and explain every progression decision.

constraints.name: Read approved direction
constraints.description: Every Action evaluates its relevant Goals, ADRs, Constraints and approved Use Cases before work.
constraints.rationale: Agents cannot implement approved intent they have not received.

constraints.name: Run exact validation
constraints.description: Every Action runs the checks named by its instruction and reports their exact outcome.
constraints.rationale: Completion must be reproducible from concrete checks.

constraints.name: Preserve clean architecture
constraints.description: Changes preserve explicit domain boundaries, single ownership and maintainable dependencies.
constraints.rationale: A local success must not create hidden coupling or duplicate truth.

constraints.name: Evidence is required for done
constraints.description: Validation may return done only with stable, independently inspectable evidence.
constraints.rationale: Provider prose is not an execution fact.

constraints.name: Use safe paths and isolated worktrees
constraints.description: Repository writes stay within the managed worktree and approved path boundary.
constraints.rationale: The active checkout and unrelated files must remain protected.

constraints.name: Meet accessibility and responsive contracts
constraints.description: Core workflows remain keyboard-operable, labelled and usable at the accepted desktop and narrow viewports.
constraints.rationale: Operator authority must not depend on pointer input, color or a wide screen.

constraints.name: No premature State progression
constraints.description: No later State or lower-priority bypass may start before every preceding gate is done.
constraints.rationale: Deterministic order is the Environment control contract.

constraints.name: No agent self-approval
constraints.description: Agents cannot approve Use Cases, Critic proposals or Refinement proposals.
constraints.rationale: Proposal authority and human decision authority must stay separate.

constraints.name: No automatic merge push release or deploy
constraints.description: Local execution never merges, pushes, publishes or deploys without a separate exact human authorization.
constraints.rationale: A local run does not grant external lifecycle authority.

constraints.name: No unauthorized external writes
constraints.description: Agents do not write to external services without explicit scoped human authorization.
constraints.rationale: Execution profiles and prompts cannot widen external authority.

constraints.name: No compatibility or dual-write paths
constraints.description: The strict target does not add migrations, compatibility readers, route aliases or dual writes.
constraints.rationale: One canonical contract keeps the pre-production system understandable and fail-closed.

constraints.name: No project workflow in platform code
constraints.description: Ballet-specific workflow identifiers and procedures do not appear in generic backend, frontend or shared platform logic.
constraints.rationale: The platform must execute arbitrary project-local Environments.

constraints.name: No fake validation or skipped failures
constraints.description: Checks are not fabricated, disabled or skipped to claim completion.
constraints.rationale: Failing evidence must remain visible and actionable.

constraints.name: No secrets in prompts or logs
constraints.description: Secrets, credentials and unredacted sensitive values never enter prompts, events or retained logs.
constraints.rationale: Immutable evidence must be safe to inspect.

useCases.name: Define project direction

examples.given: the project needs a bounded outcome
examples.when: the human maintains Goals, ADRs and Constraints
examples.then: agents receive one explicit approved decision context

failureGoals: No provider prompt becomes an alternative source of project intent
expectedOutcomes: A traceable Direction closure for authoring and execution

useCases.name: Describe and approve a Use Case

examples.given: a draft Use Case with acceptance intent
examples.when: the human approves its exact semantic hash
examples.then: the approved revision may enter an Environment

examples.given: an approved Use Case
examples.then: approval is invalidated and execution is blocked

successGoals: Only exact human-approved Use Cases are runnable
failureGoals: No stale approval survives a semantic edit
expectedOutcomes: An immutable approval record bound to one canonical content hash

useCases.name: Provide architecture decisions to agents

examples.given: an Action traces to accepted architecture
examples.when: its immutable task context is composed
examples.then: the relevant Goal, ADR, Constraint and Use Case references are available to the roles

successGoals: Architecture decisions reach every affected Action
failureGoals: No Action relies on ambient or obsolete architecture context
expectedOutcomes: A hash-bound instruction and Skill closure with stable decision references

useCases.name: Model work as an Environment

examples.given: approved work with multiple dependency stages
examples.then: the Environment exposes one deterministic progression path

examples.given: duplicate or empty State ordering
examples.then: the Environment is rejected before provider dispatch

successGoals: Work is decomposed into ordered and inspectable States
failureGoals: No freeform topology or ambiguous State order is runnable
expectedOutcomes: A strict Environment definition with unique ascending State order

useCases.name: Process State Actions by priority

examples.given: a State with multiple Actions
examples.then: it dispatches the lowest-priority-number pending Action

examples.given: an earlier Action or State is not done
examples.then: zero later Actions are dispatched

successGoals: Action selection is deterministic and gate-safe
failureGoals: No pending or blocked predecessor can be bypassed
expectedOutcomes: Ascending priority execution inside the first incomplete State

useCases.name: Define an Action

examples.given: one bounded capability is needed
examples.when: the human defines its task, evidence, retries, roles and resources
examples.then: Validation and Work receive an executable immutable composition

successGoals: Every Action is bounded, resourced and independently verifiable
failureGoals: No single Action represents the whole project
expectedOutcomes: An Action with exact Use Case references, instructions, Skills and retry limit

useCases.name: Check Action readiness

examples.given: a pending Action
examples.then: it returns only done, delegate or blocked with evidence

examples.given: insufficient or contradictory evidence
examples.then: it cannot return done

successGoals: Validation proves completion or bounds the next work before any write
failureGoals: No false done or Work-first execution

useCases.name: Delegate bounded work to a subordinate agent

examples.given: Validation returns delegate with a bounded dynamic prompt
examples.then: Work executes only that prompt in the managed worktree

examples.given: Work attempts an approval or external write
examples.then: the operation is denied

successGoals: Subordinate Work is isolated and explicitly scoped
failureGoals: Work cannot route, approve or widen its permissions
expectedOutcomes: A completed or needs-input Work outcome for Validation to postcheck

useCases.name: Retry or block an Action

examples.given: Validation rejects completed Work while retry budget remains
examples.then: one additional Work attempt receives the correction

examples.given: the final allowed Work attempt still needs retry
examples.then: the Action and exactly one Feedback entry are committed atomically as blocked

successGoals: Semantic retries are bounded and blockers stay visible
failureGoals: No provider failure silently consumes semantic retry budget
expectedOutcomes: Done, a bounded retry, or atomic blocked Feedback

useCases.name: Form the final Run Evidence

examples.given: every Environment Action is done and finalization succeeds
examples.then: a Run Evidence projects commit, artifacts, statuses, approvals and evidence

examples.given: the Environment is incomplete or blocked
examples.then: no terminal Run Evidence is invented

successGoals: The final evidence is factual, immutable and inspectable
failureGoals: No provider prose or partial run becomes a Run Evidence
expectedOutcomes: A recomputable terminal projection linked to canonical truth

useCases.name: Run scheduled quality criticism

examples.given: a disabled default Critic schedule
examples.then: no automatic provider run starts

examples.given: an enabled due occurrence with a valid lease
examples.when: Critic inspects the latest Run Evidence
examples.then: it produces at most one read-only proposal and no Feedback

successGoals: Quality criticism is scheduled, non-overlapping and evidence-based
failureGoals: No schedule overlap, write or autonomous approval
expectedOutcomes: An immutable Critic proposal awaiting a human decision

useCases.name: Approve and collect Feedback

examples.given: a Critic proposal with exact revision and hash
examples.then: exactly one provenance-bound Feedback entry is appended

examples.given: a rejected, stale or unapproved proposal
examples.then: it contributes zero Feedback entries

successGoals: Only deliberate human-approved criticism enters the Feedback Box
failureGoals: No proposal is treated as Feedback before approval
expectedOutcomes: Append-only Feedback with exact proposal provenance

useCases.name: Refine an Action and rerun immutably

examples.given: approved Feedback and a read-only exact-hash Refinement proposal
examples.when: the human approves the exact impact and apply succeeds
examples.then: one managed-worktree commit creates one immutable continuation run

examples.given: a stale preimage, forbidden path or incomplete shared Skill impact
examples.then: zero project files and zero continuation runs are created

successGoals: Approved refinement is exact, local and auditable
failureGoals: No proposal writes, partial apply or parent-run mutation
expectedOutcomes: A verified refinement commit and lineage-bound continuation run

environment.name: Ballet evidence development
environment.description: Deliver Ballet changes through approved direction, deterministic gates, Validation-led execution and immutable evidence.

states.name: Direction and acceptance
states.description: Establish accepted decision context and an exact approved Use Case closure.

actions.name: Verify Goals, ADRs and Constraints
actions.description: Reconcile the bounded initiative with accepted WHAT, WHY, architecture decisions and constraints; record trace gaps explicitly.

actions.name: Verify approved Use Cases and traceability
actions.description: Make the Use Case closure complete, exact-hash approved and traceable to measurable acceptance evidence.

states.name: Architecture and design
states.description: Define maintainable architecture, runtime contracts and accessible interaction design before implementation.

actions.name: Maintain affected arc42 sections
actions.description: Update the smallest canonical architecture views, stable IDs and links required by the approved change.

actions.name: Define domain and API contracts
actions.description: Specify strict TypeScript domain boundaries, persistence invariants and HTTP contracts without compatibility paths.

actions.name: Align evidence interaction design
actions.description: Define canonical workspaces, status semantics, approval consequences and responsive accessibility behavior.

states.name: Implementation
states.description: Implement the approved design across shared contracts, runtime persistence and user-facing workspaces.

actions.name: Implement shared domain contracts
actions.description: Implement pure strict schemas, status derivations, ordering and public DTO contracts with focused tests.

actions.name: Implement backend runtime and persistence
actions.description: Implement Validation-led control, atomic SQLite facts, recovery, permissions and governance idempotency.

actions.name: Implement frontend workspaces
actions.description: Implement factual Configure, Run, Feedback, review and Run Evidence experiences with canonical routes.

states.name: Verification
states.description: Prove runtime semantics, repository quality, security and accessible operation without skipped failures.

actions.name: Verify Action runtime semantics
actions.description: Exercise ordering, precheck, delegation, retry, blocked Feedback, restart and immutable evidence behavior.

actions.name: Verify repository build and quality
actions.description: Run the exact repository validation, test, lint, build and document checks and retain truthful evidence.

actions.name: Audit security and accessibility
actions.description: Verify request validation, actor trust, permission boundaries, secret hygiene, keyboard use and responsive layouts.

states.name: Release evidence
states.description: Assemble truthful documentation, local install/startup evidence and a human-reviewable delivery package.

actions.name: Maintain evidence documentation and traceability
actions.description: Update README, architecture status, traceability and initiative evidence only from completed checks and decisions.

actions.name: Run local install and startup smoke
actions.description: Build and install the local artifact, start a fresh strict database and verify canonical health without external writes.

actions.name: Review the delivery evidence package
actions.description: Perform conformance, risk and method-health review and hand off explicit limitations without external lifecycle actions.
